description.it: Le ventisei lettere autentiche di san Filippo Neri (1515-1595) pubblicate da Alfonso Capecelatro nei «Documenti» della sua Vita di san Filippo Neri (1879): a Francesco Vai, a san Carlo Borromeo, al cardinale Federigo Borromeo, alle monache Trievi di Firenze, a Fiora Ragni e ad altri figli spirituali, ciascuna con il sommario dell’editore. Segue una lettera al coadiutore di Bologna non compresa nelle stampe precedenti. Il testo italiano viene dalla scansione OCR e non è rivisto sulle immagini; la traduzione inglese segue lettera per lettera.
description.en-US: The twenty-six authentic letters of St. Philip Neri (1515-1595) as published by Alfonso Capecelatro in the Documents of his Life of St. Philip Neri (1879): to Francesco Vai, to St. Charles Borromeo, to Cardinal Federigo Borromeo, to the Trievi nuns of Florence, to Fiora Ragni and other spiritual children, each with the editor’s summary. A twenty-seventh letter, to the coadjutor of Bologna, which the earlier prints omit, is added in Italian. The Italian is from OCR and not proofread against the page images; the English is the translation in Antrobus’s edition of Bacci, letter for letter.
description.pt-BR: As vinte e seis cartas autênticas de são Filipe Néri (1515-1595), publicadas por Alfonso Capecelatro nos «Documentos» de sua Vida de são Filipe Néri (1879): a Francesco Vai, a são Carlos Borromeu, ao cardeal Federico Borromeu, às religiosas Trievi de Florença, a Fiora Ragni e a outros filhos espirituais, cada uma com o sumário do editor.

it.editor: Alfonso Capecelatro (La vita di S. Filippo Neri, Milano)

en-US.translator: Anonymous (Oratorian translation, ed. Frederick Ignatius Antrobus)

sources.edition: Alfonso Capecelatro, La vita di S. Filippo Neri, libri tre, Milano 1889, vol. I, Documenti, N. IV. Internet Archive scan, OCR text.
sources.description: Letters I-XXVI and the final letter to the coadjutor of Bologna, with Capecelatro’s summaries. Page furniture and hyphenation were stripped by script and obvious OCR slips corrected by a list of fixes; the text was not proofread against the scan and still carries stray OCR errors (roughly 1% of words), and a few of the editor’s footnotes may be left inline.
sources.tierEvidence: Capecelatro died in 1912; the 1889 printing is public domain everywhere.

sources.edition: Pietro Giacomo Bacci, The Life of Saint Philip Neri, ed. Frederick Ignatius Antrobus, London: Kegan Paul 1902, vol. II, Letters of Saint Philip, pp. 355-409. Internet Archive (Google) scan, OCR text.
sources.description: Letters I-XXVI with their summaries; Antrobus’s notes on the addressees are kept as footnotes. OCR cleaned by script and a list of fixes, not proofread; residual errors remain. The fragment to Tiberio is headed as such. Antrobus’s all-capitals Latin inscription quoted in a note to letter XXIV was too corrupt to keep.
sources.tierEvidence: Antrobus died in 1903; the 1902 edition is public domain everywhere.
